column4: SpatialCostSemantics.scala (EventBounds.+ / scale / hull; CostSem.add / mul / hullI)
column5: INTERVAL ARITHMETIC IS SOUND: a count in γ(i) plus one in γ(j) lies in γ(add i j); a product in γ(mul i j); k executions each in γ(i) sum into γ(mul ⟨k,k⟩ i) (the `scale` rule); the hull over alternatives contains what any alternative contains.  Upper endpoints are `WithTop ℕ`: saturation to INF is the sound direction.
THE ORDER IS CONTAINMENT: `i ⊑ j` (j.lo ≤ i.lo, i.hi ≤ j.hi) implies γ(i) ⊆ γ(j); it is transitive and the hull is an upper bound of both arguments.

column4: SpatialCostSemantics.scala (Walk(share = true) for lower endpoints, Walk(share = false) for upper; frontierEvents' MUST side; narySummBounds)
column5: LOWER BOUNDS FROM MUST FACTS, UPPER FROM MAY FACTS: an endpoint L below every admitted execution and an endpoint U above every one give an interval containing every admitted execution; ⟨0, ⊤⟩ admits everything.  The rules that produce L only read universal facts (maximal sharing, must-present keys, must-aliasing) and the rules that produce U cover every alternative (no sharing, every may-present key, every alias possibility).

RANGE NORMALISATION: the window `normalize(size, start, end)` lies in [0, size] with lo ≤ hi; (0, 0) is the identity window on a nonempty source and the empty source has the empty window; the slice `[lo, hi)` of the canonical order has exactly hi − lo elements, the full slice is the source and the empty window selects nothing.

column5: WIDENING: a widening that dominates the join is an upper bound of both its arguments, so the iteration `cur := widen(cur, nxt)` never drops a fact; the iteration stops at a post-fixpoint (`nxt ⊑ cur`).

THE FINITE-MODEL PRINCIPLE: a decidable property with no counterexample on a finite universe holds on every element of it — what the checker's zero-failure enumeration of the small universe establishes for that universe.
The exact-tier union transfer is EXACT on the small universe: γ(union#(α a, α b)) = {a ∪ b} for every pair.
The exact-tier intersection transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier subtraction transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier restriction (prefix-filter) transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier raffination (prefix-complement) transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier composition (concatenation) transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier tails-union transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier tails-intersection transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier wrap transfer is exact on the small universe.
The exact-tier unwrap transfer is exact on the small universe.

The exact-tier range transfer (the canonical-order slice under `normalize`) is exact on the small universe over eight windows including the identity, the empty, the first, the last and negative windows.
The alias short circuit `x ∪ x = x` (the same object on both sides) is exact on the small universe.
The alias short circuit `x ∩ x = x` is exact on the small universe.
The alias short circuit `x ∖ x = ∅` is exact on the small universe.

The pricing rules' containment on the dumped rows is re-checked independently: for every (operation, backend, inputs, component) row the counted total lies in [lo, hi] and no upper endpoint is infinite on a closed exact program.  The exhaustive Scala gate (SpatialCostCheck: 399360 + 11264 binary/unary rows, 36096 summarized rows, the corpus hunt) is the full enumeration; these rows are its independent spot re-check.

column3: proofs/spatial-semantic (the certified SpatialTyping transfers, corpus STATUS.tsv); SpatialDomainCheck
column5: The summarized tier REUSES the certified shape × count transfers (proofs/spatial-semantic): a summarized operation is `SpatialTyping.infer` on the two-mention term, and `SpatialDomainCheck` checks γ-containment of every summarized outcome against the reference evaluator on the finite universe.

THE EVENT SEMANTICS IS THE EXECUTORS': the compositional semantics produces the same event multiset as the instrumented executions for every constructor and backend (1148 constructor cases, the fuzzer corpus, the cornerstones).  This is the implementation-correspondence boundary T9 names; it is checked differentially, not proved.

BACKEND PRICING ↔ COUNTED SEMANTICS: every backend parameter of the pricing (Patricia envelope 2k−1, live-frontier probes, cursor reads, graph slots) is checked against the counted executions: exhaustive small-model containment, summarized declarations, the randomized hunt, the cornerstones and the geometric ladders, with zero containment failures.

THE `Long` ARITHMETIC IS THE `WithTop ℕ` ARITHMETIC BELOW 2^63: `Ivl.add`/`Ivl.mul` return the exact sum/product when it is representable and INF otherwise.  Lower endpoints never saturate in any analysed program (they are bounded by the finite inputs); a lower endpoint reaching INF would be reported as an infinite interval, never as a tight one.

column3: SpatialCostSemantics.scala (maxRounds; notes "no post-fixpoint within N abstract rounds"); SpatialDomain.scala (DomainBudget; DomainCert.widenings)
column5: TERMINATION OF THE ABSTRACT ITERATION is a checked run-time property, not a theorem: a fixpoint or system that reaches no post-fixpoint within `maxRounds` abstract rounds is reported with an INFINITE round count and a note, never with a finite bound.  Every widening applied is named in the report's certificate.

column5: THE PATRICIA SHAPE DEPENDS ON THE INTERNER'S IDS (process-dependent): a merge of two child maps with m and n keys is priced by the envelope [1, 2·(m+n)−1] Patricia visits, which holds for every id assignment; the exact visit count is not predicted.
